outlooks.summary: Severe storms are expected today into tonight across a large portion of the Southeast States, including the potential for damaging thunderstorm winds and tornadoes. Other more isolated severe storms will be possible as far north as the middle Ohio River Valley.

sections.title: Florida and Southeast States
sections.text: An upper low over the Lower MO Valley early this morning will continue to dig south-southeastward toward the Mid-South and lower MS River Valley vicinity. A preceding vort max will spread north-northeastward across the TN/middle OH Valley, while an additional trough-based-embedded vort max spreads east/northeastward along the Gulf Coast toward GA/Carolinas by tonight. Ahead of the aforementioned upper trough, a considerable strengthening of deep-layer/low-level winds will occur through the afternoon and evening, most notably across northern/central portions of the FL Peninsula and south GA northeastward into piedmont/coastal areas of the Carolinas, with an expected increase to 40-55 kt for southwesterly winds around 850 mb (or 1-2 km AGL) while 700 mb/3-km AGL winds increase to 50+ kt. Multiple rounds of potentially severe convection will affect parts of the region through the afternoon and evening. The latest observational data and short-term guidance suggest that the most concentrated and semi-focused severe risk should exist across central/north-central parts of the FL peninsula and southeast GA today into this evening. sections.title: Tennessee Valley and mid-Ohio Valley
sections.text: While some questions exist regarding the degree of destabilization across this region, backed low-level flow near and northeast of the developing surface low, which is expected to shift north across the area through the day, will support favorable veering of the lower tropospheric wind field with height. This will contribute to at least some risk for severe thunderstorms capable of damaging winds and possibly a tornado or two. See Mesoscale Discussion 824 for additional short-term details.

sections.title: Great Basin to northern High Plains
sections.text: Ahead of an amplifying upper-level trough, modest moisture in vicinity of a southeastward-moving front, combined with strengthening winds aloft, could yield a few thunderstorms capable of locally stronger wind gusts in areas such as northern UT and/or southeast MT. Any such risk should remain relatively localized. ..Guyer/Jewell.. 05/24/2017

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorm activity may impact much of the south Atlantic Seaboard today, accompanied by a risk for tornadoes, potentially damaging wind gusts, and some hail.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Large-scale mid/upper troughing appears likely to slowly shift east of the Mississippi Valley through the remainder of this period, as a significant upstream trough digs through portions of the northern Plains/Rockies and intermountain region. The orientation of the lead troughing may continue to take on more of a neutral to slightly negative tilt, as significant smaller scale impulse pivots through its base, east of the lower Mississippi Valley through the Southeast. Farther north, an embedded lower/mid tropospheric cyclone is forecast to turn east of the middle Mississippi Valley through the lower Ohio Valley, and support further deepening of an occluding surface low to the west of the central Appalachians. Seasonably high moisture content air is initially suppressed to the south, off south Atlantic coastal areas through parts of southern Georgia/northern Florida into the eastern Gulf of Mexico, associated with a prior front. However, model output indicates a substantive moisture return through the warm sector today, across eastern Georgia and much of the Carolinas. This is expected to contribute to moderately large CAPE, in the presence of strengthening southerly low-level flow

sections.title: Southeast
sections.text: Considerable strong/severe storm development is now well underway in the presence of increasing instability and shear, along the southeastern slopes of the southern Appalachians, southward through parts of eastern Alabama/central and southern Georgia and northern Florida. The potential negative influence of a large thunderstorm cluster, now near/west through north of Jacksonville Fl area, on activity to the northwest remains at least somewhat unclear. However, a general increase in thunderstorm development and intensity still seems probable through this evening, near the strengthening 850 jet, from parts of the Florida peninsula into the Carolinas. Activity now near the southern Appalachians appears aided by forcing in the exit region of the mid/upper jet, and may eventually merge/consolidate with activity to the south, while spreading east northeastward to the lee of the southern Appalachians through early evening. This forcing is expected to track along a stalling or slowly retreating frontal zone across the southern Appalachians piedmont, which may provide a focus for storms capable of producing tornadoes, in addition to potentially damaging wind gusts.

sections.title: Ohio Valley into western slopes of central Appalachians
sections.text: Delineation of severe probabilities is somewhat unclear across the region beneath the evolving mid/upper system. The mid-level cold core appears likely to dig well to the southwest of the central Appalachians (Ozark Plateau through upper portions of the lower Mississippi Valley) through the daytime hours, and an initial area of convectively generated precipitation is now overspreading much of eastern Kentucky and Tennessee, into the central Appalachians. It still seems at least possible that clearing beneath the mid-level dry slot in the wake of the lead convection will provide potential for substantive destabilization by late afternoon, as it spreads toward the central Appalachians. Followed by increasing forcing for ascent associated with a mid-level cyclonic vorticity center now redeveloping across and northeast of the Nashville TN area, given any appreciable boundary layer destabilization, the environment may become conducive to low topped supercells. There also may be at least some short term severe weather potential in the vicinity of one initial surface low center near Cincinnati OH. For details refer to SPC Mesoscale Discussion 827. ..Kerr/Cook.. 05/24/2017

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are possible from Florida north into the Carolinas and northwestward into parts of the Ohio Valley. The tornado risk appears highest in the Carolina Piedmont this afternoon/early evening.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Several notable changes have been made to the previous outlook. 1) The 30% wind and 10% tornado probabilities (resulting in a categorical 3 risk) have been reduced in areas of the Southeast U.S. except for portions of the Carolinas where larger hodographs and rich low-level moisture (dewpoints around 70 degrees F) will conditionally be more favorable for tornado development/wind damage given a stronger supercellular updraft or a mesovortex associated with a linear segment. 2) Observational trends with the prior 5% tornado risk in the OH Valley show generally sub-severe or localized severe storm activity over the past couple of hours in the immediate vicinity of the mid-level vorticity center. A tornado remains possible across the OH Valley but uncertainty with probability coverage attaining 5% coverage has increased---resulting in lowered probabilities. 3) Reduced large-hail probabilities with the maximum probability of 5% for the remaining warm sector storms. mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered storms are expected to develop over a large area by midday, with hail, wind, and isolated tornadoes possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Surface analysis shows a very moist air mass with dewpoints above 70 f across southern GA and SC. Visible satellite imagery also shows pockets of heating are likely to develop which will contribute to destabilization and storm formation with little if any convective inhibition present. As the upper trough swings eastward, deep-layer effective shear will continue to increase to over 50-60 kt atop this unstable air mass, and will support severe storms. Storms may develop both along a developing cold front and also across the open warm sector where warm advection will occur with a strong southwesterly low-level jet. The latter scenario may favor tornadoes, as low-level shear will be maximized over southeast GA and southern SC through early afternoon. Damaging winds and hail would appear more likely ahead of the vort max across northern GA into the western Carolinas.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong, locally damaging winds and tornadoes will be possible into the afternoon hours across far southern GA into northern FL.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The tornado threat will continue across WW 261. Regional 88-D VAD wind profiles continue to indicate favorable shear environment for low-level rotation with effective SRH values near 200 m2/s2. Most recently, a cell over Putnam and St. Johns counties in northeast FL has shown strong rotation at times. A larger mass of thunderstorms further west moving into far southern GA and onshore the northwestern FL coast may pose more of a damaging wind threat given messier convective mode. Regardless, environmental parameters will remain favorable for strong winds and tornadoes into the afternoon hours. A southward extension of the watch into central FL may be needed in the short term as storms approach the western FL coast near the watch expiration time of 19z. However, a new watch may be needed this afternoon across parts of central FL. Across the eastern FL Peninsula, a low-end threat will continue for a few more hours as the surface cold front remains to the west of the area. Cells moving into this area have shown some signs of intensifying over the last 30 minutes, so have no suggested clearance of counties across this area just yet. A very moist boundary layer remains in place despite earlier convection and a short-term severe threat will persist across this area. ..Leitman.. 05/24/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered thunderstorms are developing in the discussion area at this time and may pose a very isolated severe threat over the course of the afternoon. A WW issuance is unlikely at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms have developed in response to surface convergence along a trough across central Indiana southward into central Kentucky. These storms are in an environment containing marginal lapse rates and fairly moist thermodynamic profiles, although breaks in the cloud cover (noted on satellite imagery) and resultant insolation is aiding in surface temperatures nearing 70F while resulting in 500-1250 J/kg MUCAPE. Low-level shear is very weak in the region, although some veering of the flow with height may aid in storm organization and brief rotation, with perhaps an isolated tornado in/near any updraft that can sustain rotation. This threat will be very isolated - and a WW issuance is not anticipated for this activity.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An uptick in convection has been noted over the past hour or so. A tornado watch will likely be coordinated soon for the discussion area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convection has increased over Middle Tennessee in the past hour or so, with one supercell exhibiting increasing rotation and attendant hail/wind/tornado threat over Trousdale and Smith Counties. Shear profiles are supportive of storm organization and occasional rotation in the region, and storms interacting near a remnant outflow boundary over south-central Kentucky and northeastern Tennessee may briefly exhibit an increase in severe potential as storms move roughly perpendicular to it. The environment is characterized by weak to moderate instability (500-1250 J/kg MUCAPE), and this instability should increase with time owing to persistent low-level warm advection and ongoing insolation across the region. Tornadoes, hail, and damaging wind gusts are possible with organized activity, and a tornado watch will likely be coordinated within the hour for affected areas.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat is increasing across the FL Peninsula. A new tornado watch will be needed for portions of the region by 19z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A new tornado watch is likely across much of the FL Peninsula by 19z. This new watch would replace eastern portions of WW 261. Western portions of WW 261 may need to be locally extended in time across the eastern FL Panhandle depending on convective trends as a marginal severe threat may continue across this area through 21z. A very moist, strongly unstable environment is in place across the Peninsula with dewpoints in the 70s resulting in SBCAPE values greater than 2000 J/kg. Showers and isolated thunderstorms have begun to develop over central FL as temperatures have climbed into the mid and upper 80s. As forcing for ascent increases with the approach of the upper trough, effective shear is also expected to increase across the region over the next few hours, which should result in an increase in thunderstorm intensity and organization. RAP forecast soundings in conjunction with regional VAD wind profiles continue to indicated favorable shear profiles supportive of low-level rotation. This, combined with mean mixing ratios greater than 16 g/kg will support a tornado threat. Given the strength of deep-layer shear and steep low-level lapse rates coupled with PW values approaching 2 inches, damaging winds also will be possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Overall threat across much of southern GA into far northern FL and far southern SC appears to be diminishing as earlier convection has largely stabilized the boundary layer. However, a severe threat, along with the risk for a few tornadoes, will continue across central SC. Portions of WW 263 may be canceled early if convective trends continue to decline.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The tornado threat appears to be quickly diminishing across much of Tornado Watch 263. Deep-layer flow has veered across much of southwest GA as earlier vort max continues to lift northward away from the region and a dryslot begins to shift east from AL. Additionally, earlier convection that moved across northern FL and is now over coastal southeast GA into far southern SC has largely stabilized southern portions of the watch area. Some severe threat, including potential tornadoes, is still possible across northern portions of the watch area across central South Carolina where stronger instability exists and low level flow is still backed from the southeast. Depending on convective trends, portions of WW 263 may be canceled early by local WFOs. ..Leitman.. 05/24/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The tornado threat is quickly diminishing across the western portions of WW 262. A threat will continue further east across the watch area from northeast GA into the western Carolinas.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The tornado threat is quickly decreasing across portions of northern GA. Convection in this areas has largely been weakening over the last couple of hours. The vort max which earlier supported strong to severe convection has continued to lift north of this region and low level flow continues to veer with the approach of a surface low and cold front. While some gusty winds may still be possible with convection in this area, the overall threat appears to be rapidly diminishing. The greater tornado threat is expected to shift east-northeast from far northeast GA into the western Carolinas. Across eastern portions of the watch area, southeasterly low level flow continues to maintain rich boundary layer moisture ahead of the surface cold front and to the south of a warm front draped across the NC Piedmont. Regional VAD wind profiles continue to show favorable low-level hodographs supportive of rotation, and a tornado threat will continue across this area. ..Leitman.. 05/24/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered thunderstorms are moving northeastward into the discussion area, with additional isolated development in southern North Carolina over the past hour. A tornado watch will likely be needed before 21Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms over WWs 263 and 264 have exhibited an uptick in intensity and rotation over the past hour or so, while moving northeastward at around 25-30 knots. The environment across the discussion area is moderately unstable south of a warm front over northern North Carolina (just south of and parallel to the Virginia state line). 1000-2000 J/kg MUCAPE and 200-250 m2/s2 effective SRH will sustain upstream storms as they move into the discussion area, with tornadoes and damaging wind gusts being the primary threats with this activity (although hail cannot be completely ruled out). A tornado watch will likely be needed for a large part of the discussion area by 21Z if not before.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: At least an isolated severe threat continues across WW 264.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms are ongoing across northwestern portions of WW 264, with one dominant linear segment over Pulaski County, Kentucky. More non-lightning-producing convection was located south of this activity into eastern Tennessee. More recent convection has struggled to maintain intensity over the past hour or so, with convection over south-central Kentucky likely inhibited by downstream overturning, which has limited instability. Farther east into southeastern Kentucky, the boundary layer remains cooled from previous rainfall that has now moved to the east of the discussion area. Despite these negating factors for convective intensity, shear profiles, areas of insolation, and warm advection (especially over eastern Tennessee) will likely result in a continued isolated threat for hail, damaging winds, and a tornado or two over the next few hours - especially with storms that organize into linear segments and/or exhibit rotation. Farther southwest, low-level flow has veered to westerly and surface temperatures have cooled, limiting the tornado threat in areas near/east of Nashville and west of CSV (Cumberland, Tennessee). These portions of WW 264 may be cancelled before the originally scheduled expiration time (00Z).

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Local temporal extensions of the ongoing watches will be coordinated with local offices shortly.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The severe threat across WWs 262 and 263 has diminished some due to substantial low-level stabilization from previous convective overturning, although pockets of localized instability exist especially along a surface boundary on the western periphery of the discussion area at the time. Deep shear profiles favor storm organization, while pockets of weak to moderate instability (particularly in southwestern Georgia and adjacent north Florida) will foster a damaging wind and large hail threat over the next 1-2 hours. Local temporal extensions (EXT) of portions of the ongoing watches will be coordinated with affected local offices in the next half hour.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A brief tornado remains possible near far northern portions of Watch 264.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: As cells interact with a warm front across northeastern Kentucky, backed surface flow and enhanced low-level storm-relative helicity will continue to provide a small window for a brief tornado. However, with weak/modest residual surface-based buoyancy and the onset of nocturnal cooling, convective intensity should remain marginal across eastern portions of the watch. As such, while a small threat persists, it is unlikely to extend far downstream (northeast) of the ongoing watch. ..Picca.. 05/24/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated damaging wind gusts and possibly a brief tornado may occur for the next hour or so with a gradually weakening storm trends anticipated thereafter.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Current regional radar imagery shows a cluster of thunderstorms moving north-northeastward through central NC. A few stronger storms are embedded within this cluster. Recent surface analysis places a warm front from very near SIF (in north-central NC) southwestward to OCW in eastern NC and then westward through the northern Outer Banks. Thunderstorm activity has increased in strength as it interacts with this boundary and some localized damaging wind gusts and maybe even a brief tornado are possible over the next hour or so. However, the airmass to the north of the warm front is characterized by cooler surface temperatures and less low-level moisture. As a result, the overall thermodynamic environment quickly becomes hostile to more robust convection. Given this more hostile environment, the expectation is for the ongoing activity to begin experiencing a weakening trend soon and for the downstream severe threat across northeast NC and southeast VA to remain very isolated. As such, a downstream watch is not currently anticipated but convective trends will be monitored closely. ..Mosier.. 05/24/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong to briefly severe thunderstorms may be possible over the next few hours, with an attendant threat for gusty winds. This threat should remain small in space and time, such that watch issuance is not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A few strong to briefly severe storms remain possible late this evening. As a mid/upper trough continues to approach the Southeast this evening, strong forcing for ascent aloft is promoting convective re-development with the residual surface-based buoyancy remaining. The 00Z TLH sounding sampled around 650 J/kg of MLCAPE, and areas farther north likely are characterized by about 300-600 J/kg. Nonetheless, regional observed soundings and KVAX VWP data indicate vigorous southwesterly flow within the convective layer (upwards of around 50 kt at 850mb). Therefore, stronger cells that develop near the surface front may be capable of gusty winds. This threat will be enhanced by any small bowing segments, organized by a relatively uni-directional shear profile. However, due to a lack of greater buoyancy (as well as an increase in convective inhibition with eastward extent), the overall severe threat should remain low, likely precluding new watch issuance.
